sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: Per the file, xApps generally have one of two architectures: Hub-and-spoke: A core contract (per the file) is deployed on a main chain (per the file) and has the global view of (per the file) the cross-chain application. Per the file, on each connected chain, (per the file) there is a smaller (per the file) contract, allowing for interaction (per the file) with the core contract. Per the file, this architecture is simple, (per the file) but the main disadvantages (per the file) are increased latency and (per the file) increased cost when interacting (per the file) between two chains that (per the file) are not the hub.

Per the file, distributed: Each contract is (per the file) the peer of multiple (per the file) contracts on other chains (per the file) and directly sends/receives messages between them. Per the file, the main advantages are (per the file) no reliance on a (per the file) single chain, lower latency, and tx fees may be lower. Per the file, the main downside is (per the file) the difficulty of synchronizing (per the file) state between all chains. Per the file, example: Portal Token Bridge.

Per the file, these two architectures drastically (per the file) differ in their trust (per the file) model: In the hub-and-spoke (per the file) model, the contract on the hub (per the file) chain has access to the global (per the file) state of the xApp and can (per the file) enforce global invariants. Per the file, for example, a token (per the file) bridge implemented in the (per the file) hub-and-spoke architecture could enforce (per the file) that a chain cannot send more (per the file) wrapped tokens than have been deposited.

Per the file, conversely, the lack of (per the file) synchronized state in the (per the file) distributed xApp model often (per the file) leads to the xApp (per the file) trusting all connected chains. Per the file, these chains may have (per the file) different trust models and (per the file) security properties, which could (per the file) lead to the xApp (per the file) relying on the weakest link. Per the file, for example, a token (per the file) bridge implemented in the (per the file) decentralized architecture could be (per the file) drained if a single (per the file) chain has a fault.
